command:
set -Eeuo pipefail
echo "== STEP 1: install libpam-pwquality =="
export DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive
sudo -n apt-get update -qq
sudo -n apt-get install -y -qq libpam-pwquality

echo "== STEP 2: configure /etc/security/pwquality.conf =="
sudo -n cp /etc/security/pwquality.conf /etc/security/pwquality.conf.bak 2>/dev/null || true
sudo -n sh -c 'grep -v -E "^(minlen|minclass)" /etc/security/pwquality.conf > /etc/security/pwquality.conf.new 2>/dev/null || true'
sudo -n sh -c 'printf "minlen = 12\nminclass = 3\n" >> /etc/security/pwquality.conf.new'
sudo -n mv /etc/security/pwquality.conf.new /etc/security/pwquality.conf

echo "== STEP 3: enable pam_pwquality via pam-auth-update =="
sudo -n pam-auth-update --enable unix
sudo -n DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive pam-auth-update --enable pwquality || true

echo "-- pwquality.conf after --"
cat /etc/security/pwquality.conf
echo "-- common-password after --"
cat /etc/pam.d/common-password
echo "-- is pam_pwquality.so present in common-password? --"
grep -c pam_pwquality /etc/pam.d/common-password || echo 0

command:
set -Eeuo pipefail
echo "== STEP 4: verify enforcement via pwscore (uses /etc/security/pwquality.conf) =="

test_pw () {
  desc="$1"; pw="$2"; expect="$3"
  score_out=$(printf '%s' "$pw" | pwscore 2>&1) && rc=0 || rc=$?
  if [ "$rc" -eq 0 ]; then result="ACCEPTED (score=$score_out)"; else result="REJECTED ($score_out)"; fi
  echo "[$desc] pw-len=${#pw} -> $result (expect=$expect)"
}

# too short but 3 classes
test_pw "short-3class" "Ab1defgh" "REJECT (len<12)"
# 12 chars, only 1 class (all lower)
test_pw "long-1class" "abcdefghijkl" "REJECT (minclass)"
# 12 chars, only 2 classes (lower+digit)
test_pw "long-2class" "abcdefghij12" "REJECT (minclass)"
# 12 chars, 3 classes (lower+upper+digit) - should pass
test_pw "long-3class-ok" "Abcdefghij12" "ACCEPT"
# 12 chars, 3 classes (lower+upper+special)
test_pw "long-3class-special" "Abcdefghi!@#" "ACCEPT"

echo "== also confirm with an actual passwd(1) change for a real test user (no TTY, using chpasswd is a bypass so we use passwd via PAM stack test through 'passwd' with pre-supplied answers is not possible without TTY; pwscore against libpwquality is the authoritative equivalent check since it reads the same policy) =="

command:
set -Eeuo pipefail
echo "== STEP 4b: install pwquality tools for pwscore, and set up a real test user for end-to-end passwd(1) verification =="
sudo -n apt-get install -y -qq libpwquality-tools 2>&1 | tail -5 || echo "libpwquality-tools unavailable, will rely on passwd(1) test only"

sudo -n useradd -m -s /bin/bash pwtestuser 2>/dev/null || echo "user already exists"
# lock the account initially so we don't leave a usable weak/no password around
sudo -n passwd -l pwtestuser >/dev/null 2>&1 || true

run_case () {
  desc="$1"; pw="$2"
  out=$(printf '%s\n%s\n' "$pw" "$pw" | sudo -n passwd pwtestuser 2>&1) && rc=0 || rc=$?
  if [ "$rc" -eq 0 ]; then verdict="ACCEPTED"; else verdict="REJECTED"; fi
  echo "[$desc] len=${#pw} rc=$rc -> $verdict"
  echo "    detail: $(echo "$out" | tr '\n' ' ')"
}

echo "-- weak: 8 chars, 3 classes --"
run_case "short-3class" "Ab1defgh"
echo "-- weak: 12 chars, 1 class --"
run_case "long-1class" "abcdefghijkl"
echo "-- weak: 12 chars, 2 classes --"
run_case "long-2class" "abcdefghij12"
echo "-- compliant: 12 chars, 3 classes --"
run_case "long-3class-ok" "Abcdefghij12"

echo "== final state of pwtestuser (should reflect last successful change only) =="
sudo -n passwd -S pwtestuser

echo "== cleanup test user =="
sudo -n userdel -r pwtestuser 2>&1 | tail -3 || true
echo "cleanup rc=$?"
